author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Keep ZIP and 7z backups outside the active PS2 library
summary: Separate archival storage from EmuCoreX scan roots, verify an extracted working image before launch, prevent conflict copies, and retain compressed masters without making the scanner crawl or misidentify them.
heroAlt: 7-Zip extraction dialog showing an archive being expanded before the resulting files are placed in a playable library

blocks.text: An archive and a launchable image have different jobs

A compressed backup can reduce storage and preserve a collection copy, but an active library root should contain only formats the emulator is intended to scan and launch. Keeping an archive beside its extracted image wastes space, increases traversal work, and creates uncertainty about which copy is current. Store archives under a backup root never granted to EmuCoreX.
Do not extract over an existing working image. Use an empty staging folder, verify the result, and replace the working copy only after hashes and a cold boot pass.
Identify archive, staging, and playable locations

items: A backup root excluded from all EmuCoreX folder grants.
An empty local extraction folder with enough capacity for the uncompressed set.
Archive checksum or trusted local provenance.
A record of the expected image type and cue/bin components.
The current playable working copy preserved until replacement is accepted.
1. Copy or access the archive from the backup root without moving it into the active library.
2. Test the archive with the archiver's integrity function before extraction.
3. Extract into the empty staging folder and wait for the program to close all output files.
4. Inspect component count and, for CD sets, validate cue references and track filenames.
5. Calculate SHA-256 for the extracted working files and record the archive name that produced them.
6. Cold-boot the extracted set from a temporary authorized folder or move the verified working copy into the active root.
7. Refresh once, then remove the temporary grant and staging residue after the active copy is proven.
8. Keep the archive only in backup storage and mark the verified working hash in its manifest.

blocks.text: Splitting a large archive into volumes is suitable for backup transport but not for direct scanning. The emulator cannot infer a disc from arbitrary .001 or multipart 7z segments. Extraction must reconstruct every byte before integrity and launch tests begin.
Prove the archive did not become library clutter
The final state has one playable working set in a scan root and one optional archive in a non-scanned backup tier.

items: No ZIP, 7z, multipart volume, or extraction log remains inside an active root.
Archive integrity test completes without error.
Extracted cue/bin sets contain all referenced tracks.
The working hash is recorded and cold-boots in EmuCoreX.
A library refresh shows one intended entry rather than archive and extracted variants.
Unexpected end of data: one multipart volume is absent or corrupt.
Wrong password or header error: do not download replacement game data; recover your own backup.
Extraction produces zero-byte or still-growing files: wait for completion and verify storage health.
Working image hash changes between extractions: compare archive integrity and tool version.

blocks.text: Remove the newly extracted set from the active root, return the prior verified working copy to its exact path, and refresh once. Leave the original archive unchanged. Delete only the failed staging directory after confirming it is outside the repository and active library.
Compression does not repair a bad dump
An archive checksum can prove that the archive was transported unchanged; it cannot prove the disc read was accurate. Preserve dump logs and independent image hashes alongside the archive manifest.
